digest.key_takeaway:
Aether AI Studio


A local-first AI workstation: chat, an autonomous coding agent, and image/video generation in one interface.

Most AI front-ends either lock you into one provider or send everything to the cloud. Aether AI Studio lets you decide. Run models locally with Ollama or LM Studio and nothing leaves your machine. When you need more power, switch to OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini from the same UI.


GitHub: https://github.com/hankyleisplay/AetherAI-Studio

Latest release (Windows launcher): https://github.com/hankyleisplay/AetherAI-Studio/releases/latest

Current version: v4.1.1

articles.title: OpenRouter vs LiteLLM vs Portkey vs Kong: LLM Gateways in 2026
articles.summary:
LLM Gateways in 2026: OpenRouter vs LiteLLM vs Portkey vs Kong for Production Traffic

Most AI teams hit the same wall a few months after launch: the app works in the demo, but the API bill is unpredictable, one vendor outage takes the whole product down, and nobody can say which model served any given request. An LLM gateway is the layer that sits between your application and a dozen model providers, and in 2026 it has become the difference between a fragile demo and a dependable service. articles.title: What an Anthropic hiring manager stopped asking candidates to do
articles.summary:
Felix Rieseberg is an engineering manager at Anthropic. This month he wrote that he has stopped giving candidates the coding interview. His reason is short: AI can now handle the small coding challenges the interview was built from, so those challenges no longer tell him who will do well on his team.

articles.title: I Masked the User's Message and the Email Still Left: 7 Places PII Slips Out of a .NET 10 LLM Pipeline
articles.summary:
The idea is simple, and I liked it immediately. Before a chat message goes to the model, swap every email, phone number, IBAN and card for a typed placeholder like [EMAIL_1]. Keep the mapping in a per-conversation vault on your side. When the answer comes back, swap the values back in. The model still knows "this is an email, the same one as before", which is all it needs to call lookup_customer.
